imperial.name: Chicory

actions.text:
Sow

Forcing roots May–Jun. Outdoor heads Jun–Jul. Sow short rows of baby leaves in succession.

methods.text:
Sow 

Space seeds thinly in drills about ½ in. deep and cover with fine soil. Use forcing varieties such as Witloof for winter chicons; other types form outdoor heads.

1 · Lift and trim 

Lift forcing roots in November. Keep sound roots at least 1 in. across the crown (the top of the root); discard weak, badly forked or rotten ones. Trim leaves to 1 in. above the crown, keeping the growing point.

2 · Pot a batch 

Stand a few roots upright, close together, in a deep pot of moist compost, with crowns exposed. Shorten roots only if needed to fit. Store the rest horizontally in sand in a cool shed for later batches.

3 · Exclude light 

Cover with an upturned opaque bucket or large pot. Block holes in the cover and leave room for shoots. Keep in complete darkness at 50–59°F.

varieties.text:
Palla Rossa

A red, hearting radicchio with crisp leaves and a pleasantly bitter flavour. Useful for colourful salads and cooking.

Witloof

A forcing chicory grown for pale chicons. Lift mature roots and force them in darkness for a winter crop.

Variegata di Castelfranco

A variegated chicory for attractive salad leaves. Adds a different colour and form to the red radicchio selection.

Sugar Loaf

An upright, green hearting chicory for autumn salads. Specify the actual supplier's selection when choosing seed.

text:
Chicory.
DIFFICULTY
Fairly Easy
2/5
HARVEST SEASONS
Spring / Autumn / Winter

Chicory is grown in two useful ways: for green salad leaves in summer and autumn, and for pale, crisp chicons forced indoors to give fresh winter salad. The flavour is refreshing, tart and sometimes bitter, so it divides opinion, and excluding light produces paler, milder chicons. Forcing types such as Witloof are raised for their long roots, lifted in late autumn and brought into growth in dark, cool conditions; non-forcing types make larger lettuce-like heads for autumn use. The crop is generally healthy and not difficult, although forcing takes extra work and the roots are easiest to handle when grown in deep, loose soil.

Quick facts
Harvest

Oct – Mar

Germination

7–14 days

Sowing depth

about 1/2 in.

Row spacing

12 in. between rows

Yield (10 ft row)

6 lb

Ready in

About 18–30 weeks from sowing

Sow

Forcing roots May–Jun. Outdoor heads Jun–Jul. Sow short rows of baby leaves in succession.

Plant spacing

Between plants: thin to 6 in. for forcing varieties or 12 in. for non-forcing varieties

Recommended varieties
Palla Rossa

A red, hearting radicchio with crisp leaves and a pleasantly bitter flavour. Useful for colourful salads and cooking.

Witloof

A forcing chicory grown for pale chicons. Lift mature roots and force them in darkness for a winter crop.

Variegata di Castelfranco

A variegated chicory for attractive salad leaves. Adds a different colour and form to the red radicchio selection.

Sugar Loaf

An upright, green hearting chicory for autumn salads. Specify the actual supplier's selection when choosing seed.

Key risks
Slugs

Slugs can chew chicory seedlings and leaves, including beneath forcing or blanching covers.

Bolting

Cold conditions while young, drought or other growth checks can trigger premature flowering.

Rotting

Rot can develop in crowded, wet heads or roots under forcing covers.

Soil pests

Cutworms and swift moth caterpillars can damage chicory seedlings or roots.

VEGETABLE GUIDES
44
SALADS & LEAVES

Choose forcing or salad types.

Forcing varieties make winter chicons; other types give leaves and heads.

Keep forced chicons in darkness.

Light greens the shoots and increases bitterness.

Sowing & planting
Sow 

Space seeds thinly in drills about ½ in. deep and cover with fine soil. Use forcing varieties such as Witloof for winter chicons; other types form outdoor heads.

Forcing winter chicons
1 · Prepare
2 · Pot up
3 · Cover
1 · Lift and trim 

Lift forcing roots in November. Keep sound roots at least 1 in. across the crown (the top of the root); discard weak, badly forked or rotten ones. Trim leaves to 1 in. above the crown, keeping the growing point.

2 · Pot a batch 

Stand a few roots upright, close together, in a deep pot of moist compost, with crowns exposed. Shorten roots only if needed to fit. Store the rest horizontally in sand in a cool shed for later batches.

3 · Exclude light 

Cover with an upturned opaque bucket or large pot. Block holes in the cover and leave room for shoots. Keep in complete darkness at 50–59°F.

Soil & preparation
Choose sunny, fertile, well-drained soil; heavy feeding is unnecessary.
Loosen soil deeply so forcing roots grow straight and lift undamaged.
Add mature compost where humus is low. Rake a fine seedbed; feed only poor soil.
Looking after the crop
Thin baby leaves to 2 in.; use Quick facts for roots and heads.
Hoe regularly and water in dry spells, especially young seedlings. Eat useful thinnings.
Harvesting & storage
Pick green salad leaves as needed. Cut non-forcing heads in autumn; use promptly or keep cool. Protect standing crops from frost.
Chicons usually take three or four weeks of forcing. Cut or break just above the crown, leaving the root intact.
Water and cover again for a possible smaller second crop. Keep harvested chicons cool and dark to limit greening and bitterness.
Pests & diseases
Problem	What to look for	What to do
Slugs	Seedlings and covered leaves are chewed.	Inspect under covers; hand-pick where damage is significant.
Bolting	A flower stem replaces leaves.	Keep seedlings warm and water in dry spells.
Rotting	Covered heads or forcing roots become soft.	Remove rot; avoid waterlogging and check covers regularly.
Soil pests	Seedlings are cut off or roots damaged.	Inspect the soil around losses and remove caterpillars found.
Bitter chicons	Forced shoots turn green and bitter.	Keep roots and harvested chicons in darkness.
Final tips

Check dark covers for slugs and rot; keep shoots shielded from light.

Keep forcing compost moist, not waterlogged. Discard soft or rotten roots.

VEGETABLE GUIDES
See also: Growing Techniques 150
45
SALADS & LEAVES
